title: Design an ML Data Contract Platform
prompt:
Design a platform that lets teams register versioned datasets and data contracts for training, evaluation, and online feature generation. A contract declares schema, ownership, freshness, allowed use, validation rules, and compatibility expectations. Consumers must be able to reproduce an approved training or evaluation dataset even after producers publish a newer version.

Cover dataset identity and lineage, ingestion and validation, contract evolution, backfills, access policy, quality incidents, and how batch and online consumers use the same definitions without pretending they have identical latency or consistency. Include the operational metrics and failure containment strategy.

Do not design a universal query engine or a model-training scheduler.

response.placeholder: Define the immutable dataset snapshot and contract compatibility rule first.
response.reference_answer:
## Identities and ownership

A dataset has a logical name owned by a team, while each published snapshot has an immutable schema version, partition manifest, producer revision, validation report, lineage edges, allowed-use policy, and retention state. A contract is versioned separately and declares required fields, nullability, semantic constraints, freshness SLO, and compatible consumer versions. A training or evaluation run records the exact snapshot manifest and contract revision, never only the logical dataset name.

## Publish path and validation

Producers write candidate partitions to isolated storage, compute manifest/checksum metadata, and run schema, distribution, duplicate, and policy validations. A validator publishes an atomic catalog transition only when the candidate meets the contracted gates; otherwise it is quarantined with diagnostics visible to authorized owners. An outbox emits catalog and incident events after the durable transition. Consumers resolve a named approved snapshot through the catalog and receive signed, policy-scoped access to immutable files.

## Evolution and backfills

Compatibility is explicit: adding an optional field may be backward compatible, changing a field meaning is not. Contract changes require producer/consumer review and a migration window with parallel versions when necessary. A backfill creates new immutable partitions and a new snapshot; it does not silently rewrite a snapshot already used for evaluation. Online definitions may share feature transformation code or a semantic spec, but online materialization records its own watermark and freshness because it cannot promise batch completeness at request time.

## Governance and incidents

Access checks apply at discovery, metadata, and bytes. Allowed-use labels and deletion obligations propagate along lineage so a restricted source cannot be copied into an unrestricted derivative unnoticed. A quality incident marks affected snapshots and downstream runs, freezes optional promotion paths, and routes owners to decide whether to quarantine, repair, or issue a superseding snapshot. Audit logs record approvals, policy decisions, and data access without retaining unrestricted sensitive values.

## Operations

Measure validation failures by rule, publish latency, freshness/watermark lag, lineage completeness, incompatible-consumer requests, quarantine age, policy denials, backfill cost, and percentage of model runs pinned to reproducible snapshots. Alert separately on producer delay, validator failure, catalog unavailability, and online materialization lag; they require different containment actions.

## Progressive Hints

1. A logical dataset name is not reproducible training input.
2. Publish a manifest atomically after validation, not file by file.
3. A backfill creates a new snapshot.
4. Shared definitions do not make online and batch freshness identical.
